answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to verifiable thermodynamic work, much like how carbon is trapped beneath compressed shale. To mint a valid agent credential, a node must expend provable computational power equivalent to harvesting energy from a volatile gale, creating an asymmetric economic burden. If an attacker attempts to flood the network with fake entities, the cumulative financial and energetic cost scales linearly with the population, choking out malicious replication like an invasive vine choking a host tree.
